failure_modes: Visual separation in a 3-D projection is not a classifier; the split must be validated on held-out individuals
Trained on very few individuals, the features may encode identity rather than behaviour
Missing joint angles from tracking failures, if imputed naively, create spurious clusters
gloss: Train a network to predict future motion; its internal features separate behaviours it was never told about
invariants: No behavioural labels are used in training; labels are only used afterwards to inspect the embedding
Embeddings are taken from a fixed layer after training, then standardised before projection
mechanism: To find individual behavioural states without labels, train a model on a self-supervised prediction task and read its hidden layers. For ants: represent each pose as joint angles in exponential-map form (63 dimensions), take 25 observed frames at 15 fps, compress the 35-frame window (observed plus predicted) with a discrete cosine transform, and train a graph convolutional network (37 nodes, 256 hidden features, 12 residual blocks with batch norm, tanh and dropout 0.5, learnable node-to-node attention, about 2.1 M parameters) to predict the future joint angles with an L1 loss. Hook the output of the final residual block, standardise, and project with PCA: the first three components (47% of variance) already separate walking, running and antennation. A model that must forecast motion has to compress it, as in {{model_as_compression}}, and the compression aligns with behavioural state. The aim is per-agent state labels that, with network structure, let one study {{coevolution}} between individual states and collective topology.
